html:
The Warsaw Uprising was a rising of the Polish Home Army against the German occupation of Warsaw, which began on 1 August 1944 as the Soviet army neared the city and was crushed after 63 days, on 2 October.

The underground army wanted to free the capital itself before the Soviets arrived. Poorly armed fighters took much of the city but could not hold it. The Red Army stopped across the Vistula, and Stalin at first refused to let Allied supply planes land on Soviet ground. German troops massacred tens of thousands of civilians in the Wola district. About 150,000 to 200,000 civilians died. After the surrender the Germans systematically blew up most of what was left of the city. Warsaw was rebuilt after the war, its Old Town copied from old paintings. It followed the Ghetto Uprising and was part of World War II.
sum: The Warsaw Uprising was a rising of the Polish Home Army against the German occupation of Warsaw, which began on 1 August 1944 as the Soviet army neared the city and was crushed after 63 days, on 2 October.
